newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria may peg lev this week - fin min.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria may peg lev this week - fin min.

text.p: Bulgaria may peg the lev this week as part of preparations to introduce a restrictive monetary regime known as currency board, Finance Minister Muravei Radev said on Monday.
"The rate of exchange between the lev and the anchor currency could be fixed this week," Radev told reporters.
He declined to say which would be the anchor currency.
Bulgaria's interim cabinet, which stepped down on May 21, proposed the German mark as anchor in the currency board system of strict monetary control.

An International Monetary Fund mission is in Sofia now to help the new reformist government prepare the currency board which envisages matching money supply directly to the amount of foreign currency holdings.
Parliament is expected to approve on Wednesday amendments to the central bank law, adopting it to the operation of the currency board system.
The assembly has yet to appoint a new central bank management and finalise a revised banking bill.

The Fund extended its mission to Bulgaria last week to continue working with the government on the 1997 budget which has to be the backbone of the currency board sytem. The IMF said it was crucial that the budget deficit is kept to a minimum after preliminary projections showed it widening beyond what the Fund sees as a safe margin.
The IMF envisages reducing budget deficit in 1997 to 3.8 percent, while the government's preliminary estimates show a seven percent of GDP budget deficit.

Prime Minister Ivan Kostov urged over the weekend some 20 big state owned loss-making companies, which include the largest refinery Neftochim, the Bulgarian Telecommunications Company, the National Electricty Company, to cut wages in line with IMF recommendations to curb budget spending and the deficit.
